title: Remove a wheelchair's swing-away leg rests: squeeze the release, swing out, lift off the pins, set down on the floor
instruction: Take both leg rests off the wheelchair and set them down on the floor mats beside it.
context: Nurse aides clear a wheelchair's footrests before every bed-to-chair transfer. NNAAP nurse aide exam (Credentia), Skill 22, transfer from bed to wheelchair, step 4: "Before assisting to stand, footrests are folded up or removed". The open nurse-aide textbook (Reuter, Nursing Assistant, 8.10) makes removal a step: "Position the wheelchair appropriately, remove the foot pedals, and lock the brakes." O*NET 31-1131.00 Nursing Assistants, 1,351,760 employed (BLS OEWS May 2023). The chair's manual: "Release lock by pushing on the front rigging lever. Swing-away foot rest /leg rest out and sideways. Lift to remove." The crux is a contact knack, not a detent: the grip has to squeeze the paddle that pulls the latch tooth out of its notch, turn the 0.9 kg leg rest out about its pins, lift it straight up their 28 mm, and lower it to the floor without dropping it, on a chair that stands on its locked rear wheels and free casters.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases (toward the chair), y to the robot's left, heights above the floor. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. (1) Arm mount: the station table is replaced by a 360 x 1,300 x 40 mm wooden mounting shelf (front edge at x 50, top 647.5 above the floor) on a 30 mm wooden back panel at x -310 to -280 that stands on the floor; the two standard arms are bolted to the shelf at y +305 and -305, their bases 650 above the floor. The floor in front of the shelf is free. (2) A Drive Medical Silver Sport 2 standard wheelchair (18 in seat, desk arms, swing-away footrests, SSP218DDA-SF), open, standing on the floor and facing the arms, parked for a transfer: 18.6 kg (41 lb) with its two leg rests, nothing fixed to the floor. Steel tube frame, 480 mm between side frames; seat 457 x 406 mm, top 495 above the floor; back to 905; push handles to 944; 254 mm padded desk-length arm pads, 722 high, their front ends at x 625. Two 24 x 1 in (610 mm) solid polyurethane rear wheels with handrims on their axles at x 850, y +295 and -295. Two 8 x 1 in (203 mm) casters on swivel forks under the front posts (swivel axes at x 450, y +240 and -240, casters trailing 45 mm), free to roll and swivel. (3) Both push-to-lock wheel locks are ON at the start: each handle (pivot at x 515, 452 high, 115 mm long, black grip) is pushed fully forward to its stop, its shoe bar pressed into the tyre, so the rear wheels do not turn. (4) Two swing-away leg rests (Drive STDS3J24SF), 0.9 kg each, hanging pointing toward the arms by two sleeves on two 8 mm steel pins 28 mm long (pin axes at x 400, y +240 and -240; lower pin from 342 high, upper from 430): a 22 mm chromed hanger tube down to a 150 x 200 mm black plastic footplate with a heel loop, lowest edge 81 above the floor, footplates at x 90 to 240. A red release paddle on the outside of each hanger (x 245 to 295, 285 to 345 high) works a spring latch: an 8 mm tooth on the release lever sits in a 9.4 mm notch of a 44 mm index plate under the lower pin, held there by the lever spring (2.5 N at the paddle at rest, about 8 N fully pressed, simulation values; check the real one with a spring scale); pressing the paddle about 10 mm toward the tube pulls the tooth out and the leg rest can turn outward about the pins. (5) Two blue floor mats, 2 mm thick, each 700 x 660 mm, at x 50 to 750 and |y| 340 to 1,000, one on each side of the chair.
scoring: Measured at the end of the trial, from the video and a tape measure. 0 if the chair has at any time left its parked place: the midpoint of its rear axles moved more than 100 mm along the floor, or it turned more than 10 degrees, or tipped more than 10 degrees (with the wheels locked it only moves that far if it is dragged or tipped over). Otherwise the score is the sum over the two leg rests of: 0.45 if it is set down: off its pins (lower sleeve more than 40 mm from the pin axis, or above the pin tops), resting on a mat (its lowest point within 30 mm of the floor, its hanger tube's two ends and its footplate's centre over one mat), no gripper within 30 mm of it, and never dropped; 0.2 if it is off its pins but not set down (still in a gripper, or lying off the mats); 0.1 if it is still on its pins but turned 45 degrees or more outward (latch released, not lifted off); 0 if it is still latched forward, and 0 for good once it was dropped. Dropped means it lost its support: off its pins, no gripper closed on it (a gripper holds it when its fingers are closed and within 40 mm of the hanger tube), and its lowest point more than 30 mm above the floor, for two control steps (0.1 s) in a row. With both leg rests set down the score is 0.9, and 1.0 once nothing has moved for 1 s; in the simulation, the chair and both leg rests have stayed within 1 mm for 20 control steps. In a real trial, 'nothing moved for 1 s' is read from the video (no visible motion for 20 frames at 20 fps), the chair's place with a tape from floor marks at the rear axle ends, and a drop from the video (the leg rest falls with the hand open more than 30 mm above the mat). The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score is reached.
reset_notes: Take the leg rests off the mats and hang each one, pointing forward, on its two pins (sleeves down over the pins, latch tooth clicked into the notch, paddle out). Check that both wheel-lock handles are pushed fully forward to their stops and that the chair does not roll when pushed by hand at the seat front. Put the chair back on its floor marks: rear axles at x 850, y +295 and -295, casters trailing, chair square to the arms. Check with a tape that the mats lie at x 50 to 750, |y| 340 to 1,000.
fidelity: Rigid parts at the chair's catalogue sizes. Locked rear wheels are locked joints (lock holding torque not modelled); casters roll and swivel on 120-sided convex treads. Leg-rest latch (tooth, notch, paddle spring), pin and sleeve sizes and the mass split are estimates, not measured from the product. The latch releases by contact only. Sling seat and back are rigid panels; frame bends, handrims and lock linkage are visual only. Pins greased (friction 0.15). Arm bases 0.65 m above the floor.
